Subject: Data handling & support access follow-up — residency, retention, break-glass

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick follow-up with the items we promised to capture after the call so your security and ops teams have clarity. Please confirm anything I’ve misunderstood.

Summary of ask from FinCo:
- PII classification and retention policy options for user-generated content (30/90/365-day buckets).
- Data residency preference for EU vs US and what options Redwood can guarantee (hosted vs private).
- Support access model: least-privilege RBAC options, break-glass workflow, and audit trail retention for emergency escalation.
- Request for logging evidence (audit logs, break-glass access records) and SOC2 artifact pointers.

Our immediate next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Karthik and Marissa to outline a technical approach for support access and residency options.
2) We’ll attach a short draft retention SLA and a support-access matrix for you to review (attach: FinCo-Retention-SLA-v1.pdf, support-access-matrix.xlsx).
3) Proposed timeline: technical follow-up by EOD tomorrow, draft SLA by Wednesday, and a targeted security-review call next week.

Specific questions for your team:
- Are there any regulatory residency constraints (e.g., must remain in EU region for EU user PII)?
- Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption-in-use or just at-rest?
- Expected retention windows for logs vs payload data (do you need 1y+ audit retention?)

I’ll keep this thread tight. If you prefer, we can create a short mutual action plan in HubSpot.

Best,

Subject: Re: Data handling & support access follow-up — residency, retention, break-glass

Thanks, Sergio — good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: For our EU customers we need primary data residency in an EU region. For aggregated analytics, US can be OK but PII must remain in EU.
- Retention: Regulatory requires user PII retained no longer than 365 days in the EU profile, but we keep logs for 3 years for audit purposes.
- KMS: We prefer customer-managed keys for at-rest, but we are open to Redwood-managed keys for hosted non-PII buckets.
- Break-glass: Must be time-limited, require at least two approvers (programmatic + manager), and all actions must be logged and不可修改 [sic] exported to our SIEM.

I’ve attached our current support-access matrix for reference (this is internal to FinCo). Please avoid sharing the doc beyond this thread.

Next steps on our side: I’ll confirm regulatory owners and confirm specific log retention requirements for the security review.

-Alyssa
Alyssa Grant
Head of Product Security | FinCo Analytics
alyssa@finco.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T19:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & support access follow-up — residency, retention, break-glass

Thanks for the notes — quick tech plan below (high level) we can send to FinCo with a suggested implementation timeline.

Core capabilities we’ll highlight:
- Residency: Hosted API can pin model/data to region-specific clusters; for strict EU-only we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) with an EU control plane.
- Retention: We support configurable retention buckets per customer and per data type (message payload vs logs). We can offer 30/90/365-day presets; logs/audit trail retention is configurable to 3+ years via the enterprise log retention addon.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS supported with HSM integration for Private deployments; we can also provide envelope encryption for hosted.
- RBAC & break-glass:
  * RBAC: role templates (support_read_only, support_sudo, infra_admin) + time-bound roles
  * Break-glass: time-limited elevation token with mandatory approval flow; elevated sessions are recorded and immutable audit records are shipped to external S3/SIEM via signed delivery.
  * Audit evidence: immutable append-only logs, per-token traces, and exported CSV/JSON slices for eDiscovery.

Proposed internal next steps:
- Draft a short technical one-pager that maps FinCo's matrix to Redwood roles (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- Prepare a short demo showing break-glass flow and how an audit record looks (ETA: Monday).

I’ll pull the drive doc and HubSpot ticket into the thread (link below) and draft a concise recommend. Let me know if you want this to be customer-facing or a technical appendix.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Security & Platform | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
